memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, 'Tomorrow there will be a festival to the Lord.' So the next day the people rose early and sacrificed burnt offerings and presented fellowship offerings. Afterwards they sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry." - Exod 32:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read that again slowly. Aaron built an altar. He announced a festival. He even used the covenant name of God — "a festival to the Lord." Everything looked religious. Offerings were made. People came early. There was singing and feasting.

And it was completely offensive to God.

This is a warning we badly need. It is possible to attend, sing, give, and feel genuinely moved, while our lives run in a direction God never approved. Israel kept the vocabulary of worship and lost the substance of it. God had said, "You shall not make for yourself an image" (Exod 20:4) — the ink was barely dry.

Notice too where it ended: eating, drinking, and revelry. Worship shaped by our own appetites always eventually serves our appetites. When we make God in our image, we end up excusing what He forbids.

Jesus put it directly: those who worship the Father must worship in the Spirit and in truth (John 4:24). Sincerity is not enough if it is sincerely wrong. But do not read this in despair — read it as an invitation. God is not looking for better performances. He is looking for honest hearts that come to Him on His terms, through His Son.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a gap between your Sunday words and your Monday choices?
2. What in your worship might be shaped more by preference than by Scripture?
3. Where might God be inviting you to obey, not just to sing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not want the shape of worship without the reality of it. Search my heart and bring my life into line with Your Word. Amen.
